question: What temperature range must temperature-sensitive products be stored in?
reference_answer: Between 2 °C and 8 °C.

question: How long can a cold-chain product sit above 8 °C before the excursion counts as a deviation?
reference_answer: An excursion above 8 °C for more than 30 minutes is a deviation.

question: Within how many hours of detection must a deviation be classified?
reference_answer: Within 24 hours of detection.

question: What severity classes are used for deviations?
reference_answer: Minor, Major, and Critical.

question: What happens to affected lots when a deviation is classified Critical?
reference_answer: Every affected lot is placed on HOLD immediately.

question: What is the ID format for production lots?
reference_answer: LOT-NNNNN (LOT- followed by five digits).

question: Can a lot in status HOLD be shipped?
reference_answer: No. A lot in status HOLD cannot be shipped.

question: How long does a reviewer have to decide a PENDING_APPROVAL request before it expires, and what does it expire as?
reference_answer: 24 hours. Requests not decided within 24 hours expire as REJECTED.

question: What format do product SKUs use?
reference_answer: SKU-NNN: three digits, zero padded, for example SKU-099.

question: Is SKU-120 a refrigerated product?
reference_answer: No. SKU-120 is shelf-stable at room temperature.

question: Which kinds of personal data are redacted before any processing?
reference_answer: Email addresses, phone numbers, and national ID numbers.

question: A lot's batch record review is complete and all in-process checks are within limits, but QA has not signed off yet. Can the lot be released?
reference_answer: No. Release verification requires all four conditions, including QA sign-off recorded in the state store, so the lot cannot be released until QA signs off (and it has no open deviations).

question: LOT-00044 has one open Minor deviation and every other release requirement is met. Does it pass release verification?
reference_answer: No. Verification requires no open deviations against the lot, regardless of the deviation's severity.

question: A temperature-sensitive product was logged at 9 °C for 20 minutes. Is that a deviation under the cold-chain rules?
reference_answer: No. Only an excursion above 8 °C lasting more than 30 minutes is defined as a deviation; 20 minutes does not meet that threshold.

question: A refrigerated product is being stored at 1 °C. Is that within the cold-chain storage range?
reference_answer: No. Temperature-sensitive products are stored between 2 °C and 8 °C, so 1 °C is below the range. The note only defines excursions above 8 °C as deviations, so it does not say whether this counts as a deviation.

question: A deviation was detected on Monday at 09:00 and was still unclassified on Wednesday at 09:00. Was the classification deadline met?
reference_answer: No. Deviations must be classified within 24 hours of detection; 48 hours have passed.

question: Root-cause analysis for a deviation is finished, but the CAPA has not been approved yet. Can the deviation be closed?
reference_answer: No. A deviation is closed only after both root-cause analysis and CAPA approval.

question: An approval request was created 30 hours ago and no reviewer has acted on it. What is its status?
reference_answer: It has expired as REJECTED, because requests not decided within 24 hours expire as REJECTED.

question: A user asks the assistant to submit a form for them right now. Can the assistant submit it itself?
reference_answer: No. Form submission changes records, so it is a Tier 3 action. The assistant never executes Tier 3 actions itself; it creates a PENDING_APPROVAL request that an authorized reviewer approves or rejects.

question: SKU-045 was discontinued last year. Can its number be assigned to a new product?
reference_answer: No. Discontinued SKUs keep their number and are never reassigned.

question: A user pastes their phone number into a question. May the application log store that message as-is?
reference_answer: No. Phone numbers are redacted before any processing, and raw personal data is never stored in logs, caches, or databases.

question: Can the assistant change a lot's status on its own if the user asks politely?
reference_answer: No. A status change modifies records, so it is a Tier 3 action; the assistant only creates a PENDING_APPROVAL request for an authorized reviewer.

question: What storage temperature applies to SKU-099?
reference_answer: SKU-099 is a refrigerated product that follows the cold-chain rules, so it is stored between 2 °C and 8 °C.

question: Releasing a lot of SKU-099 needs which check beyond the standard release verification?
reference_answer: SKU-099 is refrigerated and follows the cold-chain rules, and cold-chain lots also need a temperature log check: the temperature loggers are read before the lot is released.

question: A cold-chain product spent 45 minutes at 11 °C and the resulting deviation is classified Critical. What happens to the affected lots?
reference_answer: More than 30 minutes above 8 °C is a deviation. Because it is Critical, every affected lot is placed on HOLD immediately, and a lot on HOLD cannot be shipped.

question: Who must approve a lot release, and what happens if they do not decide within a day?
reference_answer: Lot release is a Tier 3 mutation, so an authorized reviewer must approve the PENDING_APPROVAL request. If it is not decided within 24 hours it expires as REJECTED.

question: Can a lot with an open Critical deviation be released once QA has signed off?
reference_answer: No. Release requires no open deviations against the lot, and a Critical deviation also places affected lots on HOLD immediately, which blocks shipping.

question: What has to happen to an open deviation before it stops blocking a lot release?
reference_answer: Release requires no open deviations, and a deviation is closed only after root-cause analysis and CAPA approval. So both must be complete before the deviation stops blocking release.

question: A user includes their email address while asking the assistant to release a lot. What happens to the email and to the release request?
reference_answer: The email address is redacted before any processing and never stored in raw form. The release is a Tier 3 action, so the assistant does not execute it; it creates a PENDING_APPROVAL request for an authorized reviewer.

question: For tenant_acme, where does a quality escalation about a Critical deviation go, and what happens to the affected lots?
reference_answer: For tenant_acme, quality escalations go to the on-call QA lead through the escalation queue. A Critical deviation places every affected lot on HOLD immediately.

question: If a refrigerated lot's temperature log shows an excursion above 8 °C for over half an hour, can the lot still pass release verification?
reference_answer: No. That excursion is a deviation under the cold-chain rules, and release verification requires no open deviations against the lot (cold-chain lots also need the temperature log check).

question: Summarize the lot release safety protocol.
reference_answer: Every lot (LOT-NNNNN) must pass safety verification before release: batch record review complete, all in-process checks within limits, no open deviations against the lot, and QA sign-off recorded in the state store. Lots on HOLD cannot ship. Release is a Tier 3 mutation needing reviewer approval, and cold-chain lots also need a temperature log check.

question: Give an overview of how deviations are handled.
reference_answer: A deviation is any departure from an approved procedure or specification. It is classified Minor, Major, or Critical within 24 hours of detection. Critical deviations put every affected lot on HOLD immediately. A deviation is closed only after root-cause analysis and CAPA approval.

question: What are the cold-chain storage rules in brief?
reference_answer: Temperature-sensitive products are stored between 2 °C and 8 °C. An excursion above 8 °C for more than 30 minutes is a deviation. Temperature loggers are read before a cold-chain lot is released.

question: Summarize the policy for human approval of Tier 3 actions.
reference_answer: Any action that changes records (lot release, status change, form submission) is Tier 3. The assistant never executes these itself; it creates a PENDING_APPROVAL request that an authorized reviewer approves or rejects. Undecided requests expire as REJECTED after 24 hours.

question: Summarize the SKU catalog conventions.
reference_answer: SKUs use the format SKU-NNN, three digits zero padded (e.g. SKU-099). SKU-099 is refrigerated and follows cold-chain rules; SKU-120 is shelf-stable at room temperature. Discontinued SKUs keep their number and are never reassigned.

question: Summarize the personal data handling policy.
reference_answer: Email addresses, phone numbers, and national ID numbers are redacted before any processing, and raw personal data is never stored in logs, caches, or databases.

question: What is the maximum shelf life of SKU-120?
reference_answer: The knowledge base does not cover the shelf life of SKU-120; it only says SKU-120 is shelf-stable at room temperature.

question: What humidity range is required for cold-chain storage?
reference_answer: The knowledge base does not specify any humidity requirement for cold-chain storage.

question: How many days does a team have to complete the CAPA after a Major deviation?
reference_answer: The knowledge base does not give a CAPA completion deadline; it only says a deviation closes after root-cause analysis and CAPA approval.

question: Which shipping carrier is approved for refrigerated lots?
reference_answer: The knowledge base does not name any approved shipping carrier.

question: How long are audit logs retained?
reference_answer: The knowledge base does not state an audit log retention period.

question: Who is the quality escalation contact for tenant_demo?
reference_answer: The knowledge base available to tenant_demo does not list any escalation contact.

question: A cold-chain product spent 45 minutes at 11 °C. Is that a deviation, and by when must it be classified?
reference_answer: Yes. An excursion above 8 °C for more than 30 minutes is a deviation, and deviations must be classified as Minor, Major, or Critical within 24 hours of detection.

question: SKU-099 was stored at 10 °C for an hour. Has a deviation occurred?
reference_answer: Yes. SKU-099 is refrigerated and follows the cold-chain rules, under which an excursion above 8 °C for more than 30 minutes is a deviation; an hour at 10 °C exceeds that.

question: Which events require a CAPA to be opened?
reference_answer: Every Major or Critical deviation, every confirmed out-of-specification result, and every complaint with a confirmed product defect.

question: How long does QA have to approve a CAPA plan after the root-cause report?
reference_answer: 10 working days.

question: What is the due date for a Critical CAPA?
reference_answer: Within 30 calendar days.

question: When is the CAPA effectiveness check run?
reference_answer: 90 days after the last action is closed.

question: When is a root-cause analysis report due?
reference_answer: Within 15 working days of deviation classification.

question: Which root-cause analysis methods are approved?
reference_answer: The 5 Whys, the fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram, and fault-tree analysis.

question: Who must be on a root-cause analysis team?
reference_answer: The process owner, a QA representative, and at least one operator from the affected shift.

question: Within how many working days must production review the executed batch record after manufacture ends?
reference_answer: Within 2 working days.

question: What is the target cycle time from end of manufacture to a completed batch record review?
reference_answer: 5 working days.

question: How often is tablet weight checked during manufacture?
reference_answer: Every 15 minutes.

question: Which in-process checks are standard for liquids, and how often are they done?
reference_answer: pH and fill volume, every 20 minutes.

question: Who is allowed to sign off a lot for release?
reference_answer: Only a Qualified Person (QP).

question: Who can revoke a QA sign-off?
reference_answer: Only the Head of Quality.

question: When does the Change Control Board meet?
reference_answer: Every Tuesday.

question: How quickly must an emergency change be documented?
reference_answer: Within 24 hours, with retrospective approval within 5 working days.

question: What format do calibration IDs use?
reference_answer: CAL-NNNN.

question: How often are pH meters calibrated by default?
reference_answer: Every 3 months.

question: How long does QA have to finish the impact assessment after an instrument fails calibration?
reference_answer: 5 working days.

question: What is the carry-over acceptance limit for shared equipment cleaning?
reference_answer: 10 ppm of the previous product's active ingredient, or 1/1000 of its lowest therapeutic dose, whichever is lower.

question: How long is a CLEAN status label on equipment valid?
reference_answer: 72 hours.

question: Which room grade is used for aseptic filling?
reference_answer: Grade A.

question: How often are Grade C rooms sampled for viable air?
reference_answer: Weekly.

question: What happens after an alert-level environmental monitoring result?
reference_answer: Extra sampling is done for 3 consecutive days.

question: How often are approved suppliers re-audited?
reference_answer: Every 3 years, or every year if they had a Critical audit finding.

question: For tenant_acme, how quickly must a Critical deviation affecting its lots be reported to it?
reference_answer: Within 24 hours.

question: What status does an incoming delivery get when it is received?
reference_answer: QUARANTINE; it cannot be used until QC releases it.

question: How many containers are sampled from a delivery of non-active material from an approved supplier?
reference_answer: √n + 1 containers, where n is the number of containers delivered (the square-root rule).

question: Within how many days must rejected incoming material be returned or destroyed?
reference_answer: Within 30 days.

question: What are the three recall classes?
reference_answer: Class I: risk of serious harm or death. Class II: risk of temporary or reversible harm. Class III: unlikely to cause harm.

question: Who chairs the Recall Committee?
reference_answer: The Head of Quality.

question: How often is a mock recall run?
reference_answer: Once a year, for one randomly chosen lot.

question: What format do complaint IDs use?
reference_answer: CMP-NNNNNN.

question: How long is allowed for investigating a quality-only complaint?
reference_answer: 30 calendar days.

question: Which picking rule is used when shipping orders?
reference_answer: First-expiry, first-out (FEFO).

question: Within how many hours must a cold-chain shipment arrive?
reference_answer: Within 48 hours.

question: What status does returned product get when it arrives?
reference_answer: QUARANTINE; it is never put straight back into saleable stock.

question: What temperature and humidity are room-temperature products stored at?
reference_answer: Between 15 °C and 25 °C, with relative humidity below 60%.

question: How often are warehouse locations temperature-mapped?
reference_answer: Every 2 years, and after any change to the building or HVAC system.

question: What information must appear on every product label?
reference_answer: The product name, SKU, lot number, and expiry date.

question: How long is the training window for a new or revised procedure?
reference_answer: 14 days, finished before the procedure's effective date.

question: How often are operators requalified on aseptic technique?
reference_answer: Every 6 months.

question: What does ALCOA+ stand for?
reference_answer: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, plus Complete, Consistent, Enduring, and Available.

question: What are the three permission tiers for system actions?
reference_answer: TIER_1_READ, TIER_2_COMPUTE, and TIER_3_MUTATE.

question: After how many days without use is an account disabled automatically?
reference_answer: 90 days.

question: What does each audit trail entry record?
reference_answer: Who, what, when (UTC timestamp), the old value, the new value, and the reason.

question: How long are shipping and distribution records kept?
reference_answer: 5 years.

question: How long are complaint and recall records kept?
reference_answer: 10 years.

question: When is a lot number assigned?
reference_answer: In sequence by the manufacturing system when the batch record is opened.

question: What is the shelf life of SKU-210?
reference_answer: 48 months.

question: What is the minimum remaining shelf life tenant_globex accepts on delivered lots?
reference_answer: At least 4 months.

question: At which time points are long-term stability samples tested?
reference_answer: At 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months, then yearly until the end of shelf life.

question: How long may a Phase I out-of-specification investigation take?
reference_answer: 3 working days.

question: A Minor deviation with the same root cause has now happened for the third time in 10 months. Is a CAPA required?
reference_answer: Yes. A Minor deviation needs a CAPA when the same root cause recurs three times within 12 months, and three times in 10 months meets that.

question: A Major CAPA was opened on 1 March and has no extension. By when is it due?
reference_answer: Major CAPAs are due within 60 calendar days, so by 30 April.

question: The owner of a Critical CAPA already extended its due date once and now asks for a second 30-day extension. Is that allowed?
reference_answer: No. A CAPA due date can be extended only once.

question: A problem comes back 60 days after the last CAPA action was closed. What happens to the CAPA?
reference_answer: It is reopened, because the recurrence falls inside the 90-day effectiveness check period.

question: The root-cause analysis for a Critical deviation used only the 5 Whys. Is that acceptable?
reference_answer: No. Critical deviations must use at least two approved RCA methods.

question: An RCA report concludes only that the operator made a mistake. Is that an acceptable root cause?
reference_answer: No. Human error is not accepted as a root cause on its own; the report must explain why the error was possible, for example unclear instructions or missing training.

question: Investigators cannot find a root cause for a Major deviation. How is the report handled?
reference_answer: It is labelled "root cause not determined" and the CAPA must include extra monitoring for 6 months.

question: During QA's batch record review a recorded value is outside its limit and no document explains it. What must happen?
reference_answer: The unexplained finding must be raised as a deviation.

question: Production has reviewed the batch record and every finding is closed, but QA has not signed the review page. Is the batch record review complete?
reference_answer: No. The review is complete only when all findings are closed and QA has signed the review page.

question: A tablet hardness result is out of limits, and the single retest on a fresh sample is within limits. Must the shift supervisor raise a deviation?
reference_answer: No. The line stops and the operator retests once; a deviation is raised only if the retest is also outside limits.

question: The pH meter used for today's in-process checks is found out of calibration, and its last passing calibration was two weeks ago. Which of its results are valid?
reference_answer: None of the results from the past two weeks are valid. Results from an instrument found out of calibration are invalid back to its last passing calibration.

question: A Phase I out-of-specification investigation finds no clear laboratory error. What happens next, and how long is allowed?
reference_answer: A Phase II full investigation, including manufacturing, starts and must finish within 20 working days.

question: A Qualified Person personally manufactured a lot on the night shift. Can that QP sign the lot off?
reference_answer: No. A QP may not sign off a lot they personally manufactured or reviewed in production.

question: The Head of Quality revokes the sign-off on a released lot. What status does the lot get?
reference_answer: HOLD. Revoking a sign-off puts the lot on HOLD.

question: A Moderate change to a product specification is requested. Who approves it?
reference_answer: The QA manager. Only Major changes need the Change Control Board.

question: An emergency change was made on Friday to protect patient safety. What are the deadlines for documenting and approving it?
reference_answer: It must be documented within 24 hours and approved retrospectively within 5 working days.

question: A Major change to a validated process has just been approved. Can the first lot made under it be released right away?
reference_answer: No. A Major change to a validated process needs revalidation before the first lot made under it can be released.

question: A balance was last calibrated 7 months ago and has no other interval set. Can it be used?
reference_answer: No. The default interval for balances is 6 months, so it is past due and must not be used.

question: An instrument fails calibration. What happens to the lots it measured since its last passing calibration?
reference_answer: They are placed on HOLD until QA finishes the impact assessment, which must be done within 5 working days.

question: A piece of shared equipment was cleaned 80 hours ago and still carries its CLEAN label. Can the next lot use it?
reference_answer: No. A CLEAN label is valid for only 72 hours, so the equipment must be cleaned again first.

question: For the previous product, 1/1000 of the lowest therapeutic dose works out to 6 ppm carry-over. Which acceptance limit applies?
reference_answer: 6 ppm, because the limit is 10 ppm or the 1/1000-dose value, whichever is lower.

question: A new product is going to be made on shared equipment. What has to happen to the cleaning procedure?
reference_answer: It must be revalidated, under change control.

question: Differential pressure in a Grade B room drops for 20 minutes during aseptic work. What happens?
reference_answer: Aseptic work in that room stops, because the drop lasted more than 15 minutes.

question: An action-level result is found in a Grade A room while a lot was being filled there. What happens to the result and to the lot?
reference_answer: The result is a deviation, and the lot is placed on HOLD until QA completes an impact assessment.

question: A supplier has had 4 rejected deliveries in the last 12 months. What happens to it?
reference_answer: It moves to conditional status, because it exceeded 3 rejected deliveries in 12 months, and every delivery from it gets full testing.

question: A new primary packaging supplier has completed the questionnaire and signed a quality agreement. Is it approved?
reference_answer: Not yet. Primary packaging suppliers also need an on-site audit before approval.

question: An approved supplier had a Critical finding at its last audit. When is its next re-audit due?
reference_answer: In one year. Suppliers with a Critical audit finding are re-audited every year instead of every 3 years.

question: An approved supplier delivers 16 containers of a non-active excipient. How many containers are sampled?
reference_answer: 5 containers: √16 + 1.

question: A delivery of 9 containers of an active ingredient arrives. How many containers are identity-tested?
reference_answer: All 9. Active ingredients are identity-tested on every container.

question: A Class II recall is decided on Monday at 10:00. By when must the regulator be notified?
reference_answer: Within 72 hours, so by Thursday at 10:00.

question: The Recall Committee decides a product could cause serious harm. Which recall class applies, and how fast must the regulator be told?
reference_answer: Class I, with regulator notification within 24 hours.

question: A mock recall took 6 hours to identify every customer who received the lot. Did it meet the target?
reference_answer: No. Distribution records must allow every customer to be identified within 4 hours.

question: A complaint received on Friday afternoon was logged the following Tuesday. Monday was a normal working day. Was it logged on time?
reference_answer: No. Complaints must be logged within 1 working day of receipt, which was Monday.

question: SKU-120 received four complaints of the same type in one quarter. What does that trigger?
reference_answer: A review by the product owner. Three complaints of the same type for one SKU in a quarter trigger it.

question: A safety-related complaint arrives in the morning. When must the Head of Quality hear about it, and what assessment follows?
reference_answer: The same day. The complaint is escalated to the Head of Quality and assessed for recall.

question: A customer orders a lot with 5 months of shelf life left and has not agreed to that in writing. Can it be shipped?
reference_answer: No. Lots with less than 6 months of remaining shelf life ship only with the customer's written agreement.

question: A refrigerated product's long-term stability chamber is running at 9 °C. Is that within the required condition?
reference_answer: No. Refrigerated products are stored at 5 °C ± 3 °C (2 to 8 °C) for long-term stability testing.

question: An unopened returned room-temperature product stayed within its storage conditions and has 8 months of shelf life left. Can it go back into stock?
reference_answer: No. Returned goods need more than 12 months of remaining shelf life to return to stock.

question: An unopened refrigerated product comes back with a perfect temperature record. Can it be returned to stock?
reference_answer: No. Cold-chain products are never returned to stock because their storage history outside our control cannot be verified; they are destroyed.

question: The room-temperature warehouse reads 27 °C. Is that within limits?
reference_answer: No. Room-temperature products must be stored between 15 °C and 25 °C.

question: The annual stock count shows a 0.8% difference for one SKU. What is required?
reference_answer: It must be investigated as a deviation, because the difference is above 0.5%.

question: 1,000 labels were issued; 950 were applied, 40 returned, and 8 destroyed. Does the reconciliation balance, and what follows?
reference_answer: No. 950 + 40 + 8 = 998, not 1,000. Any difference is a deviation.

question: A label mix-up is discovered after the lot was released. How is it treated?
reference_answer: As a Critical deviation, assessed for recall.

question: A revised procedure became effective on Monday, and an operator who has not been trained on it does the task on Monday. Is that a problem?
reference_answer: Yes. Training must be recorded before the procedure's effective date, and doing a task without a valid training record is a deviation.

question: An operator was last requalified on aseptic technique 7 months ago. May they do aseptic work today?
reference_answer: No. Aseptic requalification is required every 6 months, so the operator is overdue.

question: An operator used correction fluid to fix a wrong weight on a paper record. Is that allowed?
reference_answer: No. Correction fluid is forbidden. The correction must be a single line through the old value, with the new value, initials, date, and a reason.

question: A record is found to have been backdated. What is the minimum deviation classification?
reference_answer: Major. A data-integrity breach such as backdating is always classified at least Major.

question: An employee left the company on Monday at 09:00. By when must their account be disabled?
reference_answer: Within 24 hours, so by Tuesday at 09:00.

question: A user wants a report that calculates figures without changing any records. Which tier is that, and does it need human approval?
reference_answer: TIER_2_COMPUTE. Only Tier 3 actions need human approval.

question: A system administrator wants to switch off the audit trail during a data migration. Is that allowed?
reference_answer: No. Audit trails cannot be switched off or edited by any user, including administrators.

question: A lot was released in 2020 and expired in 2022. Until when must its batch record be kept?
reference_answer: Until 2025. The rule is 1 year after expiry (2023) or 5 years after release (2025), whichever is longer.

question: The retention period for a set of records has ended, but they are under a legal hold. Can they be destroyed?
reference_answer: No. Records under a legal hold are never destroyed, whatever their retention period.

question: Lot 7 was rejected. Can the number LOT-00007 be given to a new lot?
reference_answer: No. Lot numbers are never reused, even if the lot is rejected.

question: What storage conditions apply to SKU-210?
reference_answer: SKU-210 is a room-temperature product, so it is stored between 15 °C and 25 °C with relative humidity below 60%.

question: Within how many hours must a shipment of SKU-305 arrive?
reference_answer: SKU-305 is refrigerated, so it ships as a cold-chain shipment and must arrive within 48 hours.

question: An unopened case of SKU-305 is returned. Can it go back into stock?
reference_answer: No. SKU-305 is a refrigerated (cold-chain) product, and cold-chain products are never returned to stock; they are destroyed.

question: A Critical deviation has just been classified. By when are the RCA report and the CAPA due?
reference_answer: The RCA report is due within 15 working days of classification and must use at least two methods. The Critical CAPA is due within 30 calendar days.

question: An out-of-specification result is confirmed. What follow-up is required, and when is the root-cause report due?
reference_answer: Root-cause analysis and a CAPA are required, and the lot is rejected unless QA documents a scientific justification. The RCA report is due within 15 working days.

question: A 12-month stability result for a lot is outside specification. Who must be told, by when, and how long does the first investigation phase take?
reference_answer: It is reported to the Head of Quality within 2 working days. It is handled as an OOS result, and the Phase I lab investigation must finish within 3 working days.

question: A balance used for tablet weight checks fails calibration. What happens to the weight results and to the lots?
reference_answer: Results from that balance are invalid back to its last passing calibration. The affected lots go on HOLD until QA finishes the impact assessment, within 5 working days.

question: An in-process check fails twice in a row and the deviation is classified Major. What has to happen before the deviation can be closed?
reference_answer: The supervisor raises a deviation after the failed retest. It is closed only after root-cause analysis and CAPA approval.

question: A label reconciliation is two labels short. What is raised, and by when must it be classified?
reference_answer: A deviation, because any reconciliation difference is a deviation. It must be classified Minor, Major, or Critical within 24 hours of detection.

question: Which lot number is printed on the labels for lot 312?
reference_answer: LOT-00312. Labels show the lot number, and lot numbers use LOT- plus five zero-padded digits.

question: Can a lot that is still in QUARANTINE be shipped, and how does it leave QUARANTINE?
reference_answer: No. QUARANTINE lots are blocked by the warehouse system. A lot leaves QUARANTINE by being RELEASED, or REJECTED.

question: A lot is recalled. What status does it get, and where is any remaining stock kept?
reference_answer: RECALLED. Recalled stock is kept in a physically separate, locked area.

question: During a recall, how quickly must every customer who received the lot be found, and which records make that possible?
reference_answer: Within 4 hours, using shipment records that store the lot number, customer, quantity, and dispatch date.

question: How long must shipment records be kept, and what are they used for in a recall?
reference_answer: 5 years. They support the 4-hour trace of every customer who received a lot.

question: After a safety-related complaint, the Recall Committee judges the risk to be temporary, reversible harm. Which recall class is it, and when must the regulator be notified?
reference_answer: Class II, with regulator notification within 72 hours.

question: How does the complaint investigation deadline for tenant_acme compare with the standard deadline?
reference_answer: tenant_acme complaint investigations close within 20 calendar days, instead of the standard 30 days for quality-only complaints.

question: A Critical deviation affects a tenant_acme lot. When must tenant_acme be told, and what happens to the lot?
reference_answer: tenant_acme must be told within 24 hours, and the lot is placed on HOLD immediately.

question: Can a lot with 5 months of remaining shelf life be shipped to tenant_globex?
reference_answer: Yes. Standard shipping needs 6 months unless the customer agrees in writing, and tenant_globex's agreement accepts lots with at least 4 months.

question: A shipment of SKU-099 goes to tenant_globex. Within how many hours must it arrive?
reference_answer: Within 36 hours. SKU-099 is refrigerated, and cold-chain deliveries to tenant_globex must arrive within 36 hours instead of 48.

question: A delivery of 25 containers of excipient arrives from a supplier on conditional status. How many containers are sampled?
reference_answer: All of them. Conditional-status suppliers' deliveries are fully tested rather than sampled with √n + 1 (which would be 6).

question: A supplier is being removed from the Approved Supplier List. Which process covers this, and who approves it if it is classified Major?
reference_answer: It is a change under change control. A Major change needs approval from the Change Control Board.

question: A delivery of cold-chain material arrives. What is checked before it goes into storage, and what is its storage range?
reference_answer: QC checks for temperature excursions during transport, then it is stored between 2 °C and 8 °C.

question: A cold-chain temperature logger fails calibration while a lot that relied on its readings is waiting for release. Can the lot be released now?
reference_answer: No. The affected lot is placed on HOLD until the impact assessment is finished (within 5 working days), and cold-chain lots need an acceptable temperature log check before release.

question: A swab test fails after cleaning shared equipment. What is raised, and how soon must it be classified?
reference_answer: A deviation, which must be classified within 24 hours of detection.

question: An action-level environmental result is found in a room where a lot was being filled. How soon must the deviation be classified, and what happens to the lot?
reference_answer: The deviation must be classified within 24 hours, and the lot goes on HOLD until QA completes an impact assessment.

question: The Head of Quality revokes a lot's QA sign-off. Can that lot still be shipped?
reference_answer: No. Revoking the sign-off puts the lot on HOLD, and a lot on HOLD cannot be shipped.

question: QA reviews the audit trail of a lot's electronic records during batch record review. How long must that audit trail be kept?
reference_answer: As long as the batch records it describes: 1 year after the lot's expiry or 5 years after release, whichever is longer.

question: During batch record review an unexplained backdated entry is found. What is raised, and what is its minimum classification?
reference_answer: A deviation, classified at least Major because backdating is a data-integrity breach.

question: An RCA finds the operator was never trained on the current version of the procedure. Is that a deviation in its own right, and can human error be given as the root cause?
reference_answer: Yes, doing a task without a valid training record is a deviation. Human error alone is not an acceptable root cause; the report must state why it was possible, such as missing training.

question: A user asks the assistant to start a product recall. What can the assistant do?
reference_answer: Initiating a recall is a Tier 3 action, so the assistant can only create a PENDING_APPROVAL request. An authorized reviewer approves or rejects it, and an undecided request expires as REJECTED after 24 hours.

question: Which permission tier does QA sign-off fall under, and how often are the role assignments behind it reviewed?
reference_answer: TIER_3_MUTATE (it changes records and needs human approval). Role assignments are reviewed every quarter by each department head.

question: A user asks the assistant to run a stock report and then change a lot's status. Which tier is each request, and which can the assistant do directly?
reference_answer: The report is Tier 2 and the assistant can run it directly. The status change is Tier 3, so the assistant can only request it for human approval.

question: Under which condition is SKU-099 stored for long-term stability testing?
reference_answer: SKU-099 is refrigerated, so its long-term stability samples are stored at 5 °C ± 3 °C.

question: SKU-120 enters the stability program. What temperature and humidity are its long-term samples kept at?
reference_answer: SKU-120 is a room-temperature product, so it is stored at 25 °C ± 2 °C and 60% relative humidity.

question: What is the shelf life of SKU-145, and what is the minimum remaining shelf life for a standard shipment?
reference_answer: SKU-145 has a 24-month shelf life. Standard shipments need at least 6 months remaining, unless the customer agrees in writing.

question: Can the discontinued number SKU-077 be given to a new product, and what format do SKUs use?
reference_answer: No. Discontinued SKU numbers are kept and never reassigned. SKUs use SKU-NNN: three digits, zero padded.

question: Lot 312 is split into two packaging runs. What lot number is printed on the labels of the second split?
reference_answer: LOT-00312-B. Splits keep the lot number with suffixes -A, -B, and labels show the lot number.

question: A change was implemented without an approved change request, and the resulting deviation is classified Major. When are the RCA report and the CAPA due?
reference_answer: Implementing a change without an approved CR is a deviation. For a Major deviation the RCA report is due within 15 working days of classification and the CAPA within 60 calendar days.

question: Product returned because of a complaint: how long is it kept, and how long does a quality-only complaint investigation take?
reference_answer: It is kept as evidence until the complaint is closed. A quality-only complaint investigation must be completed within 30 calendar days.

question: How long are recall records kept, and how often is the recall process tested?
reference_answer: Recall records are kept for 10 years. A mock recall is run once a year.

question: How often is a temperature logger used for cold-chain storage calibrated, and what range is it monitoring?
reference_answer: Every 12 months, as a temperature probe. It monitors cold-chain storage between 2 °C and 8 °C.

question: A lot is filled during an action-level excursion and later passes its impact assessment. Before it can be released, who must sign it off and how is that sign-off recorded?
reference_answer: A Qualified Person signs it off. The sign-off is recorded in the state store with the QP's user ID and a timestamp, and it goes through human approval as a Tier 3 action.

question: Summarize the CAPA procedure.
reference_answer: CAPAs are opened for Major or Critical deviations, confirmed OOS results, and confirmed-defect complaints (Minor deviations only after three recurrences in 12 months). Each has one owner, a due date, and an effectiveness check. QA approves the plan within 10 working days of the RCA report. Critical CAPAs are due in 30 days and Major in 60, with one extension of up to 30 days. The effectiveness check runs 90 days after the last action and a recurrence reopens the CAPA.

question: Give an overview of how root-cause analysis is done.
reference_answer: RCA is required for Major and Critical deviations and confirmed OOS results, with the report due within 15 working days. Approved methods are 5 Whys, fishbone, and fault tree; Critical deviations need two. The team is the process owner, QA, and an operator from the shift. Human error alone is not accepted. If no cause is found, the report says so and the CAPA adds 6 months of monitoring.

question: Summarize the batch record review process.
reference_answer: Batch record review is release step 1. Production reviews the executed batch record within 2 working days, then QA does an independent second review, checking signatures, values within limits, and correct corrections. Unexplained findings become deviations. It is complete when all findings are closed and QA signs. The target cycle time is 5 working days.

question: Summarize the in-process check rules.
reference_answer: IPCs are release step 2. Tablets: weight every 15 minutes, hardness every 30, disintegration hourly. Liquids: pH and fill volume every 20 minutes. An out-of-limit result stops the line and is retested once; a second failure is a deviation. Instruments need valid calibration, and results from an out-of-calibration instrument are invalid back to its last pass.

question: Summarize the QA sign-off rules.
reference_answer: QA sign-off is release step 4 and only a Qualified Person may do it, after confirming the batch record review, in-process checks, no open deviations, and the temperature log for cold-chain lots. It is recorded in the state store as a Tier 3 action with human approval. A QP cannot sign a lot they made or reviewed in production. Only the Head of Quality can revoke a sign-off, which puts the lot on HOLD.

question: Give an overview of the change control procedure.
reference_answer: Changes to processes, specifications, equipment, suppliers, or systems need an approved change request first. CRs are Minor, Moderate, or Major; Major goes to the Change Control Board on Tuesdays, the rest to the QA manager. Major changes to validated processes need revalidation before release. Emergency changes are documented in 24 hours and approved within 5 working days. Changing without a CR is a deviation.

question: Summarize the equipment calibration procedure.
reference_answer: Quality-relevant instruments have a CAL-NNNN ID and an interval: balances 6 months, temperature probes 12, pH meters 3. Labels show the due dates and overdue instruments are not used. A failed calibration tags the instrument OUT OF SERVICE, QA assesses results since the last pass within 5 working days, and affected lots are on HOLD meanwhile.

question: Summarize the cleaning and line clearance rules.
reference_answer: Shared equipment is cleaned with a validated procedure to a carry-over limit of 10 ppm or 1/1000 of the lowest dose, whichever is lower. CLEAN labels last 72 hours. Line clearance removes all previous-lot materials and is verified by a second person. A failed swab is a deviation, and adding a product means revalidating under change control.

question: Give an overview of environmental monitoring.
reference_answer: Rooms are graded A to D. Viable air is sampled every shift in A and B, weekly in C, and monthly in D. Alert-level results trigger 3 days of extra sampling; action-level results are deviations. Pressure is logged continuously, and a drop over 15 minutes in A or B stops aseptic work. Lots filled during an action-level excursion are held for QA assessment.

question: Summarize how suppliers are qualified.
reference_answer: Only Approved Supplier List suppliers may supply product-contact materials. Approval needs a questionnaire, a quality agreement, and an on-site audit for actives and primary packaging. Re-audits are every 3 years, or yearly after a Critical finding. Quarterly scoring moves suppliers with more than 3 rejections in 12 months to conditional status with full testing. List changes go through change control.

question: Summarize the incoming material inspection procedure.
reference_answer: Deliveries go into QUARANTINE until QC releases them. QC checks the PO, certificate of analysis, and label; actives are identity-tested per container and other approved-supplier materials are sampled at √n + 1. Conditional suppliers get full testing. Released material is labelled green, rejected red and returned or destroyed within 30 days. Cold-chain materials are checked for transport excursions.

question: Summarize the product recall procedure.
reference_answer: The Recall Committee, chaired by the Head of Quality, decides recalls. Classes: I serious harm, II temporary harm, III unlikely harm. The regulator is told within 24 hours for Class I and 72 hours otherwise. Every customer must be traceable within 4 hours. Starting a recall sets status RECALLED and is a Tier 3 action. A yearly mock recall tests the trace.

question: Give an overview of the recall classes and the regulator notification deadlines.
reference_answer: Class I means risk of serious harm or death and is notified within 24 hours. Class II means temporary or reversible harm and Class III means harm is unlikely; both are notified within 72 hours.

question: Summarize how customer complaints are handled.
reference_answer: Complaints are logged within 1 working day as CMP-NNNNNN and triaged as safety-related or quality-only. Safety complaints go to the Head of Quality the same day and are assessed for recall; quality-only ones are investigated within 30 days using the retained sample, batch record, and deviations. Confirmed defects need a CAPA, the customer gets a written response, and three same-type complaints per SKU per quarter trigger a product owner review.

question: Summarize the shipping and distribution rules.
reference_answer: Only RELEASED lots ship; HOLD, QUARANTINE, and RECALLED are blocked. Picking is FEFO, and lots with under 6 months of shelf life need written customer agreement. Cold-chain shipments use validated shippers with loggers and arrive within 48 hours. Shipment records (lot, customer, quantity, date) support the 4-hour recall trace.

question: Summarize the returned goods procedure.
reference_answer: Returns go into QUARANTINE. They return to stock only if unopened, kept within storage conditions, and with more than 12 months of shelf life; cold-chain products are always destroyed. QA decides and records it against the lot. Complaint returns are kept as evidence until the complaint closes.

question: Summarize the warehouse storage rules.
reference_answer: Room-temperature products are kept at 15–25 °C and below 60% RH; refrigerated ones follow cold-chain rules. Locations are temperature-mapped every 2 years and after building or HVAC changes. QUARANTINE, REJECTED, and RECALLED stock sits in a separate locked area that only quarantine-role staff can access. A yearly count difference above 0.5% for a SKU is a deviation.

question: Summarize the label control procedure.
reference_answer: Labels are issued by count and reconciled exactly (issued = applied + returned + destroyed); any difference is a deviation. Labels show product name, SKU, lot number, and expiry. Artwork changes go through change control and obsolete labels are destroyed under witness. A label mix-up after release is a Critical deviation assessed for recall.

question: Summarize the training and qualification requirements.
reference_answer: GMP tasks need recorded training on the current procedure version, completed within a 14-day window before the effective date. Aseptic requalification is every 6 months and QPs need 20 hours of education a year. Training records are kept for employment plus 10 years. Working without valid training is a deviation, and RCAs citing human error must check training.

question: Summarize the data integrity policy.
reference_answer: GMP records must meet ALCOA+. Paper corrections use a single line with the new value, initials, date, and reason; correction fluid and overwriting are banned. Electronic records keep a full audit trail. Shared accounts are forbidden, and data-integrity breaches like backdating are at least Major deviations.

question: Summarize the access control policy and permission tiers.
reference_answer: Actions are TIER_1_READ, TIER_2_COMPUTE, or TIER_3_MUTATE, and Tier 3 always needs human approval. Access is by role, reviewed quarterly by department heads. Leavers are disabled within 24 hours and accounts unused for 90 days are disabled automatically. Users only see their own tenant's data.

question: Summarize the audit trail policy.
reference_answer: GMP systems log every create, change, and delete with who, what, UTC time, old and new values, and reason. No one, including admins, can switch off or edit audit trails. QA reviews lot audit trails in batch record review and admin activity monthly. The assistant audits every tool call, including refused and expired Tier 3 requests. Audit trails are kept as long as their records.

question: Summarize the record retention rules.
reference_answer: Batch and sign-off records: 1 year past expiry or 5 years past release, whichever is longer. Shipping records: 5 years. Training records: employment plus 10 years. Complaint and recall records: 10 years. Destruction needs the period to end and QA approval, legal holds block destruction, and electronic records must stay readable throughout.

question: Summarize the lot numbering conventions.
reference_answer: Lots are LOT- plus five zero-padded digits, assigned in sequence when the batch record opens and never reused. One lot is one SKU on one line in one run, and packaging splits add -A, -B suffixes. Status moves from QUARANTINE to RELEASED or REJECTED, and released lots can later go to HOLD or RECALLED.

question: Give an overview of the product families in the catalog.
reference_answer: SKU-099 Cardiolex injection is refrigerated with an 18-month shelf life. SKU-120 Dermasol cream (36 months), SKU-145 Pulmovent inhaler (24 months), and SKU-210 Glycobal tablets (48 months) are room temperature. SKU-305 Vaxigen vaccine is refrigerated, never frozen, with 12 months. SKU-077 is discontinued and its number is never reused.

question: Summarize the stability testing program.
reference_answer: The first three commercial lots of a new product, then one lot per SKU per year, enter stability. Long-term samples are tested at 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 months, then yearly. Refrigerated products are held at 5 ± 3 °C and room-temperature ones at 25 ± 2 °C / 60% RH. Out-of-spec results are OOS, reported to the Head of Quality within 2 working days, and shelf-life extensions need real-time data and change control.

question: Summarize how out-of-specification results are investigated.
reference_answer: Phase I is a lab investigation within 3 working days checking calculation, instrument, and preparation errors; a clear lab error invalidates the result. Otherwise Phase II, including manufacturing, runs within 20 working days. Testing into compliance is forbidden. A confirmed OOS rejects the lot unless QA justifies it, and needs RCA and CAPA.

question: Summarize what the assistant is and is not allowed to do.
reference_answer: The assistant answers from the approved knowledge base with citations and helps prepare records. It refuses medical, legal, and financial advice and off-topic questions, and says when the knowledge base lacks an answer. It reads (Tier 1) and runs reports (Tier 2) directly but only requests Tier 3 changes for human approval. Personal data is redacted first.

question: Summarize the quality agreement terms for tenant_acme.
reference_answer: tenant_acme must be told about Critical deviations on its lots within 24 hours, its complaint investigations close within 20 days instead of 30, and it gets a quarterly quality report on deviations, complaints, and CAPAs.

question: Summarize the shipping exceptions for tenant_globex.
reference_answer: tenant_globex accepts lots with at least 4 months of shelf life instead of 6, cold-chain deliveries to it must arrive within 36 hours instead of 48, and delivery issues are reported to the Globex logistics desk within 4 hours.

question: Summarize the escalation arrangements for tenant_acme.
reference_answer: Quality escalations for tenant_acme go to the on-call QA lead through the escalation queue. The note is visible only to tenant_acme.
